mainTopic: How to read רב's ruling on a husband's inheritance, and who collects a dead man's deposit, loan or produce
overview: Earlier, רב said: 'The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but not for his reason,' about a husband who gives up his right to inherit his wife. The גמרא tries several readings of this statement. Each one is checked against רב's own ruling about אונאה and against his exact wording. In the reading the גמרא keeps, רב agrees that the husband still inherits. For רב, though, ירושת הבעל is only דרבנן, and the condition fails because the חכמים gave their laws the strength of Torah law. A challenge from רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's משנה about returning a family graveyard is answered: there, רב was only explaining that תנא's view. Then a new משנה asks who gets a dead man's deposit, loan or loose produce when his wife, a creditor and his heirs all have claims. רבי טרפון says it goes to 'the weakest', and רבי עקיבא says it goes to the heirs, because there is no mercy in judgment. The גמרא explains why the משנה lists both a loan and a deposit, gives two meanings of 'the weakest', and explains why רבי עקיבא mentions only the surplus.

steps.title: Does רב really hold that a condition against the Torah is valid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier reading of רב from his own ruling in a case of אונאה. There, רב said a condition against Torah law does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב really think such a condition holds? But we learned: if someone sells on condition that the buyer has no claim of אונאה, רב says the buyer still has the claim, and שמואל says he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier way of explaining רב. It brings a case where רב clearly holds that a condition against the Torah is void.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanation assumed רב lets a husband's condition override the Torah's inheritance law. But in the אונאה case, a seller tried to cancel the Torah's protection against overcharging, and רב said the buyer keeps his claim anyway. So for רב, a condition against the Torah does not work, and the earlier reading of him cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: His condition stands and works
Overcharging or underpaying in a sale; the Torah forbids it
On condition that
But it was stated (introduces an Amoraic statement used as a challenge)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב consistently holds that a condition cannot cancel a Torah law. That forces the גמרא to reread his statement about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: And does רב hold that his condition is valid?
But it was stated:
One who says to his fellow:

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לְךָ עָלַי אוֹנָאָה,
phrases.english: 'On condition that you have no claim of overcharging against me,'

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: יֵשׁ לוֹ עָלָיו אוֹנָאָה.
phrases.english: רב said: He does have a claim of overcharging against him.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵין לוֹ עָלָיו אוֹנָאָה.
phrases.english: And שמואל said: He has no claim of overcharging against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַב תְּנָאוֹ קַיָּים? וְהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier explanation of רב's ruling, which was given before this section begins
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רב holds a condition against Torah law is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the אונאה case, רב rules that a condition against Torah law is void. That contradicts the assumption.

steps.title: Second explanation: רב agrees the condition is void but disagrees about inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that a condition against the Torah is void. Yet רב still rules that the husband does not inherit, so he does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב meant: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said a condition against the Torah is void, but not for his reason. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that if she dies, he inherits her. רב holds that if she dies, he does not inherit her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to read רב's statement so that it fits his ruling about אונאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, רב agrees with the principle 'a condition against the Torah is void.' But he reaches a different practical result: the husband does not inherit. The idea is that רב sees this condition as not truly against the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah
His condition is void
But not for his reason
He inherits her

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Rather: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: who said: One who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah,
his condition is void; but not for his reason,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר:
phrases.english: for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds:
if she died, he inherits her,
and רב holds: if she died, he does not inherit her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reinterpreting רב's statement
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of which part of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view רב accepts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב rejected the principle that a condition against the Torah is void
steps.terutzMaskana: רב accepts the principle, but differs on the outcome: the husband does not inherit

steps.title: That explanation reverses רב's own words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the second explanation means 'his reason, not his ruling.' That is the opposite of what רב actually said.
steps.simpleTranslation: That would be 'following his reason, but not his ruling'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second explanation because it does not fit רב's exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said 'the הלכה is like him, but not his reason.' In the second explanation, רב shares רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's principle (his reason) but disagrees with his result (his ruling). That is backwards from what רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his practical ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two parts apart. 'טעם' is the reason or principle, and 'הלכה' is the final practical result. רב claimed to follow the result, not the reason.

phrases.english: This is following his reason and not his ruling!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מִטַּעְמֵיהּ וְלָא כְּהִילְכְתֵיהּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second explanation
steps.kashyaTarget: The second explanation of רב's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It flips רב's words: it agrees with the reason and disagrees with the ruling, while רב said the reverse.

steps.title: Third explanation: same result, but רב voids even conditions against rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רב agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's result that the husband inherits. He differs on the reason: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל voids only conditions against Torah law, while רב voids even conditions against rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב meant: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that if she dies, he inherits, but not for his reason. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that only a condition against Torah law is void, so a condition against rabbinic law works. רב holds that even a condition against rabbinic law is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third explanation of רב's words, built to fit his wording and his ruling about אונאה. The next step rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the practical result: despite his condition, the husband still inherits. The claimed difference is in the reason. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל voids only a condition against Torah law, which implies a condition against rabbinic law stands. רב voids even a condition against rabbinic law.

keyTerms.meaning: In a matter of Torah law
In a matter of rabbinic law
Even

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading would fit רב's ruling about אונאה. But as Step 5 shows, it makes רב agree with both the reason and the ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which does not match his words.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Rather: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
who said that if she died, he inherits her,
but not for his reason,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר
phrases.english: for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds
that in a Torah matter his condition is void,
which implies that in a rabbinic matter his condition is valid.
And רב holds that even in a rabbinic matter
his condition is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דְּאָמַר אִם מֵתָה יִירָשֶׁנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected second explanation with one that fits רב's wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: same result, different and broader reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב shares רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's principle but disagrees on the outcome
steps.terutzMaskana: רב shares the outcome (he inherits) and voids even conditions against rabbinic law

steps.title: If רב only adds a detail, he fully agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the reading just offered makes רב agree completely with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, both in reason and in ruling, with רב only adding a detail. That does not fit רב's wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: This would be fully in line with his reasoning and his ruling, and רב is just adding to it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the reading just offered. In that reading, רב would agree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on everything and only add a small detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's statement is worded as agreeing with the ruling but not with the reason, so it signals a real difference. A reading where רב follows both the reasoning and the ruling and only adds something erases that difference. So the reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: according to his reasoning
according to his ruling (his halachic result)
adds (a further detail)

phrases.english: This is according to his reasoning and according to his ruling,
and Rav is merely adding!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי כְּטַעְמֵיהּ וּכְהִילְכְתֵיהּ הוּא, וְרַב מוֹסִיף הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the preceding reading of רב's words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in which רב follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason and ruling and only adds a detail.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading רב fully agrees, so his wording that signals a difference becomes pointless.

steps.title: Same result as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, different reason
steps.stepSummary: Final reading: רב rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that the husband inherits. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, ירושת הבעל is from the Torah, so a condition against it fails. For רב, it is דרבנן, yet the condition still fails because the חכמים gave their laws the strength of Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read רב this way: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said that if she died he inherits her, but not for his reason. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that ירושת הבעל is from the Torah, and anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah, his condition is void. רב holds that ירושת הבעל is from the רבנן, and the חכמים strengthened their words like Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final explanation of רב: same ruling as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but a different reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the husband inherits even though there was a condition. They disagree on why. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs ירושת הבעל to be from the Torah, while רב says even a rabbinic law cannot be cancelled by a condition, because the חכמים made their laws as strong as the Torah's.

keyTerms.meaning: a husband's right to inherit his wife
from the Torah
from the Rabbis
one who makes a condition against what the Torah says
his condition is void
strengthening, reinforcement

steps.whatToRemember: רב and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agree that the husband inherits. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: because ירושת הבעל is from the Torah. רב: it is only דרבנן, but rabbinic laws were given Torah-level strength, so a condition cannot cancel them.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב rejects רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling. He accepts the ruling and rejects only the reason.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Rather: the halakha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
who said: if she died, he inherits her,
but not for his reason,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר
phrases.english: for Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds
the husband's inheritance is from the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: and anyone who stipulates against what is written in the Torah —
his condition is void.
And Rav holds: the husband's inheritance is rabbinic,
and the Sages gave strength to their words
like those of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דְּאָמַר אִם מֵתָה יִירָשֶׁנָּה, וְלָאו מִטַּעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading with the final one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading of רב's statement: agreement in ruling, disagreement in reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב fully follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and only adds a detail.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב agrees that the husband inherits but bases it on rabbinic law being reinforced like Torah law, not on ירושת הבעל being from the Torah.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רב can hold that ירושת הבעל is דרבנן. It quotes a משנה: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says a husband who inherits his wife must return the property to her family and deduct part of the money for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב really hold that ירושת הבעל is דרבנן? But we learned in a משנה: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says, one who inherits his wife must give it back to the family members and take off part of the money for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רב's view that ירושת הבעל is only דרבנן. It brings a משנה, and its point will become clear in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea in the last step was that רב sees ירושת הבעל as rabbinic. Now the גמרא tests that idea against a משנה whose rule seems to mix Torah and rabbinic features. This step only quotes the source; the problem inside it is explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: but we learned in a משנה (introduces a challenge)
a תנא quoted in the משנה
he must return (the property)
and he deducts
money, monetary value

phrases.english: And does Rav hold that the husband's inheritance is rabbinic?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: But we learned: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
one who inherits his wife,
must return it to the family members,
phrases.notes: This means her family. He gives her inherited field back to them in the יובל year.

phrases.english: and deduct for them from the money.
phrases.notes: They pay him for the land, but he takes off part of the price, so he gets only some of its value.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב סָבַר יְרוּשַּׁת הַבַּעַל דְּרַבָּנַן? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the premise introduced in step 6, that רב holds ירושת הבעל is דרבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's position that ירושת הבעל is דרבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about returning a wife's inheritance with partial payment will be shown to raise a problem about how ירושת הבעל is understood. The full argument continues in the next steps.

steps.title: The old puzzle: Torah law or rabbinic law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls its earlier discussion of the משנה. If רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא holds ירושת הבעל is from the Torah, why return the land? If it is דרבנן, why does the husband get any money?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: what does he hold? If he holds ירושת הבעל is from the Torah, why must he return it? And if it is דרבנן, what is the money for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back an earlier discussion that showed the משנה's rule is puzzling either way. This sets up the next move in the challenge against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband's inheritance were from the Torah, it would be a real inheritance, and inheritances do not go back in יובל. If it were only rabbinic, the land would belong to her family by Torah law, so they should not owe him anything. Neither option fits both parts of the משנה. Step 9 gives רב's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: and we discussed it (recalls an earlier analysis)
what does he hold?
why?
what is their purpose? what are they doing here?

phrases.english: And we discussed it: what does he hold?
If he holds the husband's inheritance is from the Torah,
why must he return it?
phrases.notes: A real Torah inheritance stays with the heir and does not go back at יובל.

phrases.english: And if it is rabbinic,
what is the money for?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Unpacks the משנה quoted in step 7 by recalling the earlier analysis of it, as groundwork for the challenge to רב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא holds that ירושת הבעל is from the Torah or from the רבנן, since each option clashes with part of his ruling.

steps.title: רב explains: the husband returns a family graveyard
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא holds ירושת הבעל is from the Torah. The case is a family graveyard, and the husband returns it only to spare the family shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא really holds that a husband inherits his wife by Torah law. The case is where his wife left him her family's burial ground. Because it would shame the family, the רבנן said the husband should take its value in money and give the graveyard back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8 by quoting רב's own explanation of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 asked why the husband returns the land if he inherits by Torah law. רב answers that he really does inherit by Torah law. The return is a special rabbinic fix for one kind of property, a family graveyard, so the family is not shamed.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (keeping the original assumption)
Graveyard, burial ground
A flaw or shame to the family
Take the value in money and give the property back

steps.confusionAlert: Returning the graveyard does not mean the husband did not inherit. He inherits fully by Torah law. The return is only an exception for this one kind of property.

phrases.english: And רב said: Actually, he holds
phrases.notes: "He" here is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, the תנא from the משנה quoted in Step 7.

phrases.english: that the husband's inheritance is from the Torah,
and the case is where his wife left him a graveyard as an inheritance,
because of shame to the family,
the Rabbis said he should take its value in money and give it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר יְרוּשַּׁת הַבַּעַל דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8's question by explaining what case the משנה is about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ירושת הבעל is from the Torah. The return applies only to a family graveyard, a rabbinic rule to avoid family shame.

steps.title: What the husband deducts: his wife's grave
steps.stepSummary: רב explains the words "deduct from the money": the husband keeps back the value of his wife's own grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "he deducts for them from the money" mean? He deducts the value of his wife's grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רב's explanation by explaining the משנה's words 'he deducts for them from the money': why the husband does not get the full price of the graveyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the husband takes payment for the graveyard and returns it. Here the גמרא explains why he takes off part of that payment: the deduction is the price of the plot where his wife herself is buried. So the money adjustment is tied to her grave, not to a general split of the land.

keyTerms.meaning: He deducts, subtracts
The value of a grave plot

phrases.english: And what does "he deducts for them from the money" mean?
The value of his wife's grave.
phrases.notes: A husband has to bury his wife, so the price of her own plot comes off what he is paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי ״יְנַכֶּה לָהֶן מִן הַדָּמִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's explanation by defining the משנה's phrase about deducting money.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The deduction is the value of the wife's own grave plot.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows how seriously family graves are protected
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that even if a man sold his family grave plot, his family may still bury him there against the buyer's will. This supports רב's family-shame idea. It also closes the challenge: רב clearly said ירושת הבעל is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: if someone sells his grave, the path to his grave, his standing place, or his eulogy place, his family members may come and bury him there even against the buyer's will, because of family shame!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב's point that family shame is strong enough to override ownership of grave property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא proves that the Rabbis protect family graves even against a sale. That makes רב's graveyard explanation solid. The closing exclamation also brings back the challenge from Step 7: רב himself said ירושת הבעל is דאורייתא, which contradicts Step 6, where רב treated it as דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
His standing place, where people stand to comfort mourners
His eulogy
Against his will

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source that family honor in burial can override a normal sale. It is the base for the graveyard exception.

phrases.english: As it is taught: One who sells his grave,
or the path to his grave, his standing place, or the place of his eulogy,
the members of his family come and bury him there
against the buyer's will, because of family shame!
phrases.notes: The exclamation mark is the punch line: so רב does say ירושת הבעל is from the Torah! That is the question from Step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: הַמּוֹכֵר קִבְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's family-shame explanation and closes the challenge that רב holds ירושת הבעל is דאורייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That family shame justifies forcing the return of grave property, as in רב's explanation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: family members may bury a relative in a grave he sold, even against the buyer's will.

steps.title: רב was only explaining רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב was explaining רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's reasoning, not his own. רב himself does not hold that ירושת הבעל is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב was saying this according to the reasoning of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge from Step 7. רב's explanation was only about what רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Explaining a תנא's view does not mean you agree with it. So רב can still hold, as in Step 6, that ירושת הבעל is דרבנן. The final reading of רב stands.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his (someone else's) reasoning
He does not hold that way

steps.whatToRemember: רב rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that the husband inherits, but for רב ירושת הבעל is דרבנן. His Torah-law explanation was only a way to read רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.

phrases.aramaic: רַב לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: רב was speaking according to the reasoning of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא,
but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge built in Steps 7 to 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the statement explains another's view, not the speaker's own.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רב explained that ירושת הבעל is דאורייתא, that must be his own view.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was only explaining רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. He personally holds ירושת הבעל is דרבנן.

steps.title: New משנה: who gets a dead man's deposit or loan
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a man dies, leaving a wife, a creditor and heirs, and others are holding his deposit or loan. רבי טרפון says it goes to the weakest (כושל) of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone died and left a wife, a creditor and heirs. He had a deposit or a loan in other people's hands. רבי טרפון says: it should be given to the weakest of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: several people have claims on a dead man's money, and the money is held by others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife (for her כתובה), the creditor, and the heirs all want the same money. רבי טרפון settles it by giving it to the party in the weakest position.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה
Creditor, someone owed money
Deposit, an item left with someone for safekeeping
Loan
Weak, in a weaker position

phrases.english: משנה: One who died and left a wife,
and a creditor, and heirs,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה לוֹ פִּקָּדוֹן אוֹ מִלְוָה בְּיַד אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: and he had a deposit or a loan in the hands of others,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: יִנָּתְנוּ לַכּוֹשֵׁל שֶׁבָּהֶן.
phrases.english: רבי טרפון says: they should be given to the weakest one among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁמֵּת וְהִנִּיחַ אִשָּׁה וּבַעַל חוֹב וְיוֹרְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון: the deposit or loan goes to the weakest of the claimants.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: no mercy in judgment, the heirs get it
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. Judgment follows the law, not mercy. The money goes to the heirs, because everyone else must swear before collecting, and the heirs do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: we do not show mercy in judgment. Instead, it is given to the heirs. All the others need an oath to collect, but the heirs do not need an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי עקיבא's opposing view and his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, a judge follows who has the stronger legal right, not who is needier. The wife and the creditor can only collect after an oath, while the heirs need no oath, so the heirs' claim is the strongest.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not show mercy in judgment
Heirs
Oath

steps.whyThisMatters: "אין מרחמין בדין" is a basic rule of בית דין: the law decides the case, not pity for one side.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְרַחֲמִין בַּדִּין,
phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: we do not show mercy in judgment,
rather, they should be given to the heirs.
For all of them need an oath,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the wife and the creditor. Anyone collecting from heirs must swear first.

phrases.english: but the heirs do not need an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְרַחֲמִין בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי טרפון in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: the money goes to the heirs, who need no oath, while the other claimants do.

steps.title: Detached produce goes to whoever grabs it first; רבי טרפון on the surplus
steps.stepSummary: If the dead man left harvested produce, whoever takes it first keeps it. If the wife or creditor took more than they were owed, רבי טרפון says the extra goes to the weakest of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he left produce already cut from the ground, whoever takes hold of it first acquires it. If the wife took more than her כתובה, or the creditor more than his debt, then about the extra: רבי טרפון says it is given to the weakest of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case: produce that is already harvested and lying loose. It also asks what happens to any extra that someone grabbed beyond what they were owed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With loose produce, the משנה rules that whoever takes hold of it first acquires it. If the wife or creditor took more than they were owed, someone has to decide who gets the extra, and רבי טרפון gives it to the weakest party.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce already cut or picked from the ground
Whoever comes first acquires it
The surplus, the extra beyond what was owed
The weak one, the one in the weaker position

phrases.english: If he left produce detached from the ground,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the man who died, from the case of the wife, creditor and heirs in step 13.

phrases.english: whoever takes them first acquires them.
If the wife acquired more than her marriage contract,
or the creditor more than his debt,
the surplus:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: יִנָּתְנוּ לַכּוֹשֵׁל שֶׁבָּהֶן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says: it is given to the weakest of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִנִּיחַ פֵּירוֹת תְּלוּשִׁין מִן הַקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new case: loose produce, and the surplus someone grabbed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loose produce goes to the first one who takes it. According to רבי טרפון, any surplus goes to the weakest party.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא gives the surplus to the heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says a court does not rule out of pity. The surplus goes to the heirs, because the others need an oath to collect and the heirs do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: we do not show mercy in judgment. It is given to the heirs, because all the others need an oath, and the heirs do not need an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי עקיבא's opposing view on the surplus. It uses the same reasoning he gave in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה itself repeats רבי עקיבא's words, this time for the extra produce. The heirs are in the strongest legal position, since they inherit without swearing. The wife and creditor can only collect after an oath, so the extra goes back to the heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not show mercy in judgment; the ruling follows the law
An oath
Heirs

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a mistaken repeat of step 14. The משנה really says רבי עקיבא's words twice: once for the deposit or loan, and again here for the surplus produce.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְרַחֲמִין בַּדִּין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: one is not merciful in judgment,
rather, it is given to the heirs.
For all of them need an oath,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means everyone collecting from the heirs, like the wife and the creditor.

phrases.english: and the heirs do not need an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְרַחֲמִין בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the view that argues against רבי טרפון's ruling on the surplus.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The surplus goes to the heirs, because they collect without an oath.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention both a loan and a deposit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed both examples, a loan and a deposit. One example should have been enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need it to teach a loan, and why do I need it to teach a deposit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by asking about the wording of the משנה. It is setting up an explanation that both examples are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 the משנה said the dead man's property was 'a deposit or a loan' held by others. The גמרא assumes the dispute is the same in both cases, so it asks why the משנה did not give just one example.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it to teach? (a question about extra wording)
A loan
A deposit, something left with someone for safekeeping

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Why do I need it to teach a loan,
why do I need it to teach a deposit?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנֵי מִלְוָה, לָמָּה לִי לְמִיתְנֵי פִּקָּדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה, starting with its wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה gives two examples, a loan and a deposit, when one seems enough.

steps.title: If only a loan were taught, רבי טרפון might agree about a deposit
steps.stepSummary: Both are needed. With a loan alone, we might think רבי טרפון rules as he does only because a loan is spent. With a deposit, which still exists, he might agree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If it taught only a loan, we would say רבי טרפון rules this way there because a loan is given to be spent. But a deposit, which still exists as it was, we would say he agrees with רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer: each example teaches something. Here it shows why the deposit case is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan is spent by the borrower, so what is owed is only a debt to pay back, not a specific item. That makes it easier to give it to the weakest party. A deposit is a real object belonging to the dead man, so it looks more like the heirs' property. The deposit case teaches that רבי טרפון disagrees even there.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; both teachings are needed
It was given to be spent
It still exists as it was

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if it had taught only a loan,
in that case Rabbi Tarfon says his ruling,
because a loan is given to be spent.
But a deposit, which still exists as it was,
I would say he agrees with Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי תְּנָא מִלְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The deposit case is needed to show that רבי טרפון disagrees even when the object still exists.

steps.title: If only a deposit were taught, רבי עקיבא might agree about a loan
steps.stepSummary: With a deposit alone, we might think רבי עקיבא gives it to the heirs only there. For a loan, he might agree with רבי טרפון. So both examples are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it taught only this, we would say רבי עקיבא rules this way there, but in the other case we would say he agrees with רבי טרפון. So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by showing the other side: why the loan case is needed. It ends by repeating 'it is necessary.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This' is the deposit and 'the other' is the loan. A deposit is clearly the dead man's own item, so we might think רבי עקיבא gives the heirs only that. The loan case shows that רבי עקיבא gives it to the heirs even when only a debt is owed.

keyTerms.meaning: He agrees
In that other case

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives both examples on purpose. In each case one of the two Sages might seem to agree with the other, and listing both shows they disagree in both.

phrases.english: And if it had taught only this,
in this case Rabbi Akiva says his ruling,
but in that other case,
I would say he agrees with Rabbi Tarfon.
So it is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי תְּנָא הָא, בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 18 by explaining why the loan case is needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The loan case is needed to show that רבי עקיבא disagrees even when there is only a debt.

steps.title: What does 'to the weakest' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי טרפון meant by 'the weakest.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'to the weakest' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of רבי טרפון's word. It is setting up two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The weakest' is unclear. It could mean weakest in legal standing or weakest in life situation. The גמרא needs to know who actually gets the money under רבי טרפון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? What does it mean?

phrases.english: What does 'to the weakest' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לַכּוֹשֵׁל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה's choice of examples to the meaning of רבי טרפון's word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who counts as 'the weakest' in רבי טרפון's ruling.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: the one with the weakest proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says 'the weakest' means the party whose proof, meaning his document, is weakest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says: to the one who is weakest in proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer explains 'weakest' as weakest in legal proof, not weakest in life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, the money goes to whoever has the weaker claim on paper, such as the one whose document has the later date. That person would have a harder time collecting elsewhere, so רבי טרפון gives him the extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Proof, here the document backing the claim
The one weakest in proof

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says:
To the one who is weakest in proof.
phrases.notes: This is the one whose document is weaker, such as one with a later date, so it can collect from less property.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אוֹמֵר: לַכּוֹשֵׁל שֶׁבִּרְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The weakest' means the one with the weakest document.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the wife's כתובה, for the sake of favor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says 'the weakest' means the wife's כתובה, so that women will look favorably on marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: to the wife's כתובה, because of favor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer: 'the weakest' is always the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first view, this one does not depend on whose document is weaker. The wife always gets the extra, because the Sages wanted women to feel secure and favorable toward marriage. This is called חינא.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife's marriage contract payment
Favor; so that women will look kindly on marriage

steps.whatToRemember: There are two meanings of 'the weakest' in רבי טרפון's view. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says it is the one with the weakest document. רבי יוחנן says it is always the wife, because of חינא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
To the wife's marriage contract,
because of favor.
phrases.notes: This means so that women feel secure and willing to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לִכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה, מִשּׁוּם חִינָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 20 that differs from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The weakest' means the wife, whose כתובה is favored because of חינא.

steps.title: The same argument already appears among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The argument about 'the weakest' matches a תנאים dispute. רבי בנימין says it means the one with the weakest proof. רבי אלעזר says it means the wife's כתובה, so that women will look favorably on marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of the תנאים. רבי בנימין says: the money goes to the one whose proof is weakest, and that is the proper way. רבי אלעזר says: it goes to the wife's כתובה, so that women will find favor in marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two explanations of 'the weakest' from Steps 21–22 were already argued about by earlier sages, the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי בנימין matches רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: 'the weakest' means whoever has the weakest document. רבי אלעזר matches רבי יוחנן: 'the weakest' means the wife and her כתובה. So the later אמוראים are following two older opinions. They are not inventing a new argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute of the תנאים, the earlier sages of the משנה period
The weak one, the one who is stumbling
Proof; here, the legal document backing a claim
Proper, fair
Favor, appeal; here, making marriage attractive to women

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read 'the weakest.' (1) The party with the weakest proof: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, following רבי בנימין. (2) The wife's כתובה: רבי יוחנן, following רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between תנאים:
רבי בנימין says:
It goes to the one who is weakest in proof,
and that is the proper way.
רבי אלעזר says: it goes to the wife's כתובה,
because of favor, so that women will want to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Anchors the אמוראים' argument from Steps 21–22 in an earlier argument among the תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The two explanations of 'the weakest' from Steps 21–22.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא-style argument between רבי בנימין and רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Why does רבי עקיבא mention only the surplus?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the משנה's case of detached produce. It asks why רבי עקיבא talks only about the surplus going to the heirs, since by his view all of the produce belongs to the heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If he left detached produce.' According to רבי עקיבא, why mention specifically the surplus? All of it also belongs to the heirs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, detached produce. It then challenges the wording of רבי עקיבא's opinion there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the deposit case, רבי עקיבא gives everything to the heirs. So for detached produce he should also give all of it to the heirs, not only the extra beyond the debts. Why, then, does his opinion in the משנה speak only about the 'surplus'?

keyTerms.meaning: Produce already picked or cut from the ground
Surplus, the extra left over beyond what was owed
Why specifically this? (asks why a narrow case was mentioned)
Heirs

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'If he left detached produce.'
And according to רבי עקיבא, why mention specifically the surplus?
All of it also belongs to the heirs!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, מַאי אִירְיָא מוֹתָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the detached-produce case in the משנה, after finishing the discussion of 'the weakest.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי עקיבא's opinion in the משנה's detached-produce case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא's general view gives everything to the heirs. So limiting his statement to the surplus seems unnecessary or misleading.

steps.title: True, he only said 'surplus' to match רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that for רבי עקיבא all of the produce goes to the heirs. He used the word 'surplus' only because רבי טרפון had said 'surplus.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. But since רבי טרפון said 'surplus,' רבי עקיבא also said 'surplus.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by admitting the point. The word 'surplus' in רבי עקיבא's opinion is just borrowed from רבי טרפון's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing about רבי עקיבא's law changes: all the produce goes to the heirs. The narrow wording is only a matter of style. He answered רבי טרפון in רבי טרפון's own terms.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, it is indeed so (the גמרא agrees with the question)
Since; because (here: since the other side used this wording)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, all of the detached produce goes to the heirs. The word 'surplus' in his opinion only echoes רבי טרפון's wording.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי עקיבא agrees that whoever grabs the produce first gets to keep it. He mentions only the surplus because of how the argument was worded, not because his law is limited to it.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
but since רבי טרפון spoke about the surplus,
he too taught his ruling about the surplus.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, וְאַיְּידֵי דְּאָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן מוֹתָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 24 by agreeing with it and explaining the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreement plus a stylistic explanation: the wording follows the other opinion's phrasing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי עקיבא says 'surplus,' maybe he only disputes the surplus and lets the first person who grabs the produce keep it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא gives all the produce to the heirs. He said 'surplus' only to match רבי טרפון's wording.
